question: Will Alex Michelsen win the 2026 Men's US Open?
description:
The 2026 U.S. Open tennis tournament is scheduled for August 23 - September 13, 2026.

This market will resolve to the player that wins the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed player to win the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament per the rules of the tournament, the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the 2026 U.S. Open Men’s Singles Tournament is cancelled, postponed after October 31, 2026, or there is otherwise no winner declared within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the U.S. Open (https://www.usopen.org/index.html); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Carlos Alcaraz’s return from a four-month wrist injury as defending champion, paired with Jannik Sinner’s pre-tournament knee withdrawal, has driven trader consensus toward his 58% implied probability at the 2026 US Open. The Spaniard has looked sharp in early rounds on hard courts, tightening his grip on the market after recent wins that signal regained form. Alexander Zverev sits second at 22.8% after capturing the French Open and reaching the Wimbledon final, bolstered by a relatively favorable draw and proven five-set resilience despite tough early matches. American contenders Ben Shelton (8.6%), Frances Tiafoe (4.3%), and Learner Tien (4.2%) reflect strong recent results and home-crowd support, while deeper longshots like Alexander Blockx and Karen Khachanov remain limited by ranking and head-to-head history against the top tier.
